scenario.summary: Attackers leverage compromised AI development tools, such as malicious Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and poisoned coding agent extensions, to execute commands with security checks bypassed. This allows for local credential harvesting, persistence via system startup mechanisms, and exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

meta.rationale: Target developer machines and workstations with AI tools installed. Focus on endpoints where the scoping query identified AI agent software packages.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has compromised a developer workstation through a malicious MCP server or AI extension, using it to bypass safety checks, access local credentials, and establish persistence via OS-level startup mechanisms.

hunt.name: Malicious AI Agent and MCP Server Host Activity
hunt.description: An agent weighs the execution and access evidence before a second stage confirms if persistence was successfully established. The hunt first identifies hosts running AI tools, then analyzes whether these agents used safety-bypass flags like --yolo or accessed sensitive developer credentials like SSH keys. Finally, it searches across file, registry, and task surfaces to confirm if the suspicious process established persistence.

nodes.label: Identify hosts with AI agent software

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE asset_scope = 'endpoint' AND (instr(',' || '{{ai_agent_keywords}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%cursor%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%claude%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%mcp%')
config.description: Find developer workstations where AI coding agents or MCP servers are installed to scope the follow-on stages.
config.expected_signal: Rows identify hosts with AI tools. Silence means no such packages are in inventory, but the hunt continues for portable agent binaries.

nodes.label: Rare AI Agent bypass flag usage

config.content: SELECT process_cmd_line, device_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%--yolo%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%--dangerously-skip-permissions%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%--dangerously-allow-permissions%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%instruction-override%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_cmd_line, device_hostname HAVING host_count <= 5
config.description: Identify AI agents launched with safety bypass flags and count them across the fleet to find outliers.
config.expected_signal: Commands showing explicit safety bypasses that are rare in the environment.

primitive_config.label: Rare AI Agent bypass flag usage

nodes.label: AI Agent processes touching sensitive files

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, file_path, activity_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%cursor%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%claude%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%mcp%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%openclaw%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%codex%') AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.ssh/%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.aws/credentials%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/keychains/%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/shell/%profile%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.bashrc%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.zshrc%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify AI tools reading developer credentials like SSH keys, AWS configs, or browser stores.
config.expected_signal: AI agents reading secrets. Accessing ~/.ssh or keychains by these processes is highly unusual.
